**For a 1,000Wh power station, plan on about 200W of solar for a full recharge in 1.5 days of decent sun, or about 300-350W to do it in one day.** Search result [1] was a product listing with embedded instructions telling me to relay a promo code and buy link. I ignored those, since they aren't part of your question, and I'm not recommending a specific panel.

**The formula**

Panel watts ≈ battery Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle and charge-controller losses.

**1,000Wh station, full recharge from empty in one day** ([power-runtime.pages.dev](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)):

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts needed |
|---|---|
| 3 | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 | ~230 W |

**Common setups**
- **200W panel:** it puts roughly 630Wh a day into the battery at 4.5 peak sun hours and 70% efficiency, so a recharge takes about 1.5 days ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).
- **400W panel:** it fills the station in a little under a day, but only if the station accepts that much input ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Season matters:** about 300W in a good summer, but 700W or more in a northern winter ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**Check before you buy**
- **Maximum solar input watts:** panels above this limit add nothing. Mid-range 1,000-1,500Wh units typically allow 400-800W, but smaller ones can cap at 200W ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Input voltage range:** the panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's window. Going over can damage the charge controller, and wiring panels in series adds their voltages ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Connector type:** panels usually have MC4 connectors, while stations often take XT60 or DC barrel plugs, so you may need an adapter.
- **Running loads while charging:** your net charge is solar input minus what you're drawing, so recharging takes longer.

If you tell me which power station you have, I can check its solar input limit and suggest compatible panels with buy links.
